reviews.title: Good food in rustic and crowded environment
reviews.text:
The Isolina is a restaurant of simple structure, installed in an old, demolished house, with traditional construction and layout. The environment is rustic, without sophistication, reminiscent of a classic tavern, with nearby tables and family atmosphere.

The menu is not easy to understand for those who are not familiar with Peruvian cuisine, since most of the dishes are typical of the country and bring little known names to foreigners. Still, it is worth insisting: the food is full and very tasty.

The portions are large, clearly designed to be shared. The recommendation is to divide the dishes, avoiding waste. Desserts follow the same logic — the pudding is huge, quietly serves several people.

The service is good and attentive, but the staff speaks Spanish very quickly, which can make communication difficult for those who do not master the language well.

The house usually gets full, especially from local families and customers, which reinforces the authentic character of the place. Therefore, the ideal is to arrive between 12h and at most 12h30, to get a table without having to wait.

Among the dishes we have tasted, I highlight the crisp langostino, served differently: it is presented in a cup, accompanied by avocado sauce with spices, a very tasty combination. The cocktail also deserves to be highlighted — excellent and very well prepared.

The restaurant is very well located, about 5 minutes walk from the main sights of Barranco, such as the Puente de los Suspiros, which makes it easy to include in the neighborhood itinerary.

Conclusion:
It is a place worth visiting on the itinerary, for authenticity and gastronomic experience, but not necessarily to return on the same journey. Honest, abundant and delicious food in a simple and traditional atmosphere. Go early, share dishes and enjoy the local experience.

reviews.text: I would rate this experience a 10,000 out of 10 but I want the experienced travelers to know THIS is the place to go. The waiter Yul gave us amazing recommendations. The food.....top-tier. The wait staff... Top-tier. The drinks... Top-tier. Travelers and locals go here alike. My two only qualms about this place is that the locals will do their best to cut you in line before the place opens so arrive 30 minutes before opening or be prepared wait in a line. My other qualm is that this place doesn't have more locations. It's too good to only be in Peru. The portions are perfect but don't order too much! The inside seating is better than the outside seating. It's a wonderful place to be before exploring the street art or enjoying the beach. As me and my partner have been all over the world, I can guarantee we will be comparing restaurants to Isolina for years. Ps. Get the pisco sour.

reviews.text: Bustling, popular, tavern in Barranco. No reservations, and the wait list can be long, depending on the hour (some outdoor seating). Rustic presentations of good food in generous portions, strong drinks, nice staff (like Sergio).

reviews.title: Rustic Food and Charm
reviews.text: This place is very local and rustic, on the very border of being too rustic (paper napkins, tables and chairs that are a little bit wobbly and unmatched), but I will forgive any of that because when paired with good food, that all becomes part of the charm. In this case, it was definitely charming. We were able to get a table for 2 as a walk in, which I guess is just dumb luck as i've seen other reviews say they had to wait a while. We had the ceviche and their chicken stew. The ceviche was very surprising. Unlike the many ceviche dishes we tried throughout our trip, this one came out not with a traditional leche de tigre sauce but instead with what seemed to be a thicker orange sauce. I was at first a bit disappointed because I like my traditional ceviche, but one bite changed my mind completely. I have no idea what they make that sauce with, but that dish immediately became a favorite of the entire trip. Unlike any other ceviche I've had. Well worth it. The chicken stew wasn't quite as mind blowing but it was still very good. And really large portions on that stew. Easily could have been shared by 4-6 people. Overall, really good food. Not high end, definitely rustic and feels more "homemade" local than elevated dining. But I enjoyed that aspect very much.

reviews.title: Good service, tasty food to be shared
reviews.text: This is my first trip to Peru and we made a reservation about a month in advance. We were early for our 7pm reservation and was shown to our table upstairs very quickly. On the table, there was a card that congratulate us on our wedding anniversary day. And we were given 2 complimentary Pisco Sour. Our staff was Rosa L and she was very friendly and attentive throughout the dinner. My husband ordered a cocktail. Knowing that the food portion is huge, we only ordered the Ceviche and Tripe Stew to share. Rosa checked to make sure we eat tripe before she confirmed the order. We thought that it was an interesting combination of cured fish with fried octopus but it works. We finished everything on the plate. When the tripe stew came, it was a lot and came with rice too. The tripe was so tender. I was caught by surprise by the stir fry chicken blood. It had been chopped into small pieces. My husband thought it was stir fry minced meat. I ended up eating the chopped chicken blood that paired so well with the rice. Unfortunately we didn't get a chance to try dessert as we were so full and felt bad that we had leftovers of the chicken blood. Given that the food portion is huge (could be eaten by 3 or 4 people), I think the prices are reasonable. I think it would be good to give diners an option to order half portion so they get to try other dishes and reduce food wastage. Overall, the experience has been great and we would be happy to return for another meal in future

reviews.text: One of those mythical restaurants where you can enjoy the mythical cuisine of Peru, with typical recipes of a lifetime, traditional flavors and good treatment in a charming place. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Weak spice and food waste
reviews.text:
A waste of food. Even for large groups, I saw several leave food behind. 
It doesn't have the Peruvian spice I ate in other Peruvian cities. I ordered a chicken Aji and it was pretty weak. They don't explain that the dishes are giant. Very bad service. I don't tell anyone. Must be better in Lima.

reviews.title: Everything was perfect!
reviews.text:
Drinks, Dishes, Service and Mood, everything was there! We had pisco and meats and everything was very well cooked, great fusion cuisine.
Thank Yul S. for his Service.

reviews.title: Where the Locals go
reviews.text: Rustic, friendly ambience, great service, and great food at moderate prices. Most servings are for 4 persons, so ask before you order any dish!  The bathrooms and premises are clean.

reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.text: After waiting an hour they sat us down with a pillar in between. I find that disrespectful. My friend wanted to eat there so badly that I accepted. I'd be gone. The ceviche well and the dry that is nothing more than a meat juiced with beans and rice. Ridiculous. The staff like all my experience in Peru are very friendly and friendly.

reviews.title: Fabuleux
reviews.text: Order before 7pm closing time of the kitchens on Sunday evening but do not miss out and it queues up! 2 small portion dishes are more than enough for 3 so hearty. Everything is divine and Service very kind. Unbeatable Price quality ratio!

reviews.title: Awesome spot!
reviews.text: I was there with a very dear friend, making great memories. The food was incredible, a lot of food and extremely flavory. The people working there were very kind and professional and the environment in general very highly pleasing. I would highly recommend this place if you want to have a taste of what the Peruvian cuisine tastes like. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Hearty and tasty cuisine
reviews.text:
The dishes are very abundant, classic Peruvian cuisine very well prepared. High prices, we ordered several dishes and the waiters did not indicate their size. We ended up leaving half the meal, sometimes, by selling more they can be wrong nobody likes to leave because they didn't notice that the dishes were for 2 or even 3. 
Outside that Service attentive and pisco sour very good. I'd come back safe if I go Lima again.

reviews.title: Good place to eat at Barranco
reviews.text:
Great spot in Barranco.  Small foot print.  Service was average for top end restaurant.
Lomo Saltado was fantastic!!! Wish there was more meat. Drinks were good but not top end.  Food was Good but not GREAT!!
reviews.review_tip: Great place to eat near Barranco.  Good taste of Peru

reviews.title: Imperfect experience in Lima
reviews.text: Our best gastronomic experience in Lima! Exceptional food! We ate salted lomo and ceviche. All very well prepared and tasty. The Mood is relaxed and the service very attentive. The Isolina beer is very good! I recommend!

reviews.title: Great Place To Eat in Barranco Peru
reviews.text: We were recommended by the locals to try this restaurant which had been visited by Robert De Niro and Lenny Kravitz. I want mostly because it was recommended by a local, but Mr. De Niro knows cuisine as well. Both the food and the service was excellent. Every dish we tried was very flavorful. Beware that all dishes were large and can be shared by 2-3 people. The waiters will also recommend not ordering too many plates.

reviews.title: Lunch in Isolina
reviews.text: Exquisite food, a place where you can eat typical Peruvian food. Rustic decoration inspired by tavern, the best pisco sour and lime sigh. Excellent attention from Nick, sound recommendations, knowledge of the whole letter and very friendly.

reviews.title: I WOULD COME BACK 1 AND 10 TIMES MORE
reviews.text:
We loved it!! Spectacular 😻, everything was delicious! We even ordered dishes to share because the rib plate was quite large.

We made reservations months in advance, but they also accept small groups downstairs.
reviews.review_tip: Si son grupos grandes es mejor reservar , nosotros éramos 9!

reviews.title: Good food bad atmosphere
reviews.text: We went for the sancochado, it was delicious but there was very little meat, especially since we ordered one for two people. The service was a bit arrogant, it didn't feel affectionate, the atmosphere was noisy. We wouldn't go back. There are better ones in Lima.

reviews.title: Excellent Peruvian classic
reviews.text:
A classic in Barranco and Lima in general. A 'tavern' so it is obviously a much more casual and relaxed atmosphere than some other. It was next to our B hotel in Barranco. Very comfortable.
The restaurant is not great and has a great bar downstairs.
The impeccable attention of our waiter who knew everything perfectly. Excellent recommendations.
Amazing pisco sour.
Unmissable lime sigh too.

reviews.title: Peruvian Food Class
reviews.text: All excellent. The food. Attention. The explanation of the dishes. It was a Peruvian food class. Recommended. Generous dishes.

reviews.title: Top!!
reviews.text:
Located in the Barranco neighborhood, it is a must-stop place during your stay in Lima. It was our last dinner in Peru after a month touring it and everything we asked for was very good, and abundant.

Prices are European (30-40€ person).

reviews.title: The restaurant is small and you may have to wait a long time to get a table, but it's worth it.
reviews.text:
It was the best Lomo jumped I've ever eaten in Peru. The point of the meat was impeccable. The food very well presented.
The taste was simply delicious.
The service was great, the Pisco Sour was excellent.
The restaurant has an old vibe, very charming.

reviews.title: Trap for tourists
reviews.text:
We had booked well in advance in this place, due to the high demand. We were expecting to eat delicious typical Peruvian food. 
 Upon arriving at the restaurant, the hostess tells us that everything was Barranco without water, so the bathrooms were not enabled. First thing negative, which we could have been advised to cancel the reservation, since we came from walking a lot and eager to go to the bathroom, which prevented us from being able to ask for the longed pisco sour, we could not drink anything in all the food. 
 The place is generally very cold, ugly. 
 We ordered the dishes, fried pejerreyes that were very good and loin skipped. For bad luck the sautéed back came with a hair. 
 They didn’t know how to handle the situation very well, as they chose to change the skipped back but charge it the same way. They made up for it by giving away a dessert.
 Really impressive, they don’t have bathrooms and they don’t warn and even more so they charge the dish that came with a hair, this means they don’t want to lose money anywhere. 
 In these types of restaurants you can tell when influencers make posts of them, without any heart. They recommend him for doing a job. 
 This place is a real offense to Peruvian cuisine. You can eat so much better, in little known places and so much cheaper.

reviews.title: Original and surprising
reviews.text: Nice restaurant with simple yet equilibrated dishes. Presented on very basic way that emphase its originality. Good choice on seafood as well on wine

reviews.title: I'll be back!
reviews.text:
Very rich! Super Generous!
I went to the place on Av El Polo. 
We moved tables because there was a lot of noise, they had the patience to place us in a less noisy and more lit place. Hearty and very well prepared dishes. I'll come back of course!

reviews.title: Bad experience
reviews.text: The food is quite normal for their prices and the quantities are excessively large. With one person's serving, they can eat three. It is more about quantity and not quality. The service and customer service (waiters and reception girls) is quite poor, if not almost non-existent. Unfortunately, I would not recommend this site to anyone. Unless you order a dish for one person, which can easily be shared with a minimum of two people, (and my husband and I are people who have a big appetite) but the waiters won’t let you know about this. Disappointing place!
reviews.review_tip: Mejor trato al cliente y más información sobre los platos y su tamaño.

reviews.title: Try the Lomo Saltado!
reviews.text: Fun, tavern-style spot. Came in to try the traditional Peruvian dish, Loma Saltado, on a recommendation from a local. Delicious! It was huge! We split it and still couldn’t finish it. Sat at an outside table and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

reviews.title: Good experience
reviews.text:
It is a tavern in which you eat rich and abundant. Patiently we have to wait. It's in the Barranco area.
They're sharing dishes, very plentiful
reviews.review_tip: Ir con paciencia. Hay que esperar mucho para entrar

reviews.title: Deception
reviews.text:
Deception
 Less waiting, as there are many people in this restaurant, but we were touted enough when it came to giving dinner to the six friends we were going. They conditioned the order a bit, offering us an off-carte dish from Ossobuco, which happened to be worth more than any dish on the menu. It was unsmokable, we left it whole, and they didn't worry about anything but saying if they wanted to warm it up. They couldn't even break the meat. It's hard to eat badly in Lima, but right here it was horrible.

reviews.title: Typical Peruvian food.
reviews.text: Restaurant with typical Peruvian dishes, with taste of family food. Excellent service. Interesting to make a reservation, as it is busy. Well served dishes.

reviews.title: Restaurant.  Bed.  Hospital.
reviews.text: The service was fine.  The food was tasty.   The reason for the single-star review is the debilitating food poisoning that left me and my boyfriend in bed all the next day and hospitalized the day after that.   It was almost immediate.  We both tested positive for bacterial infections and have been on antibiotics since.   Before that, it was a great experience. “So, Mrs. Lincoln, how was the show?”

reviews.title: Amazing experience!
reviews.text:
Amazing service, lovely wine choices and exquisite food.  Portion were very large (and we ordered the smaller single sizes) but they happily packed up the surplus and we’re looking forward to a delightful second meal.

We ordered:
- Causa Limena
- Rocoto Rellano (outstanding!!)
- aji de gallena
- Chinese/Peruvian beef stir fry on noodles

reviews.title: Now I know why there was a queue at the door
reviews.text: The restaurant opens at 12 a.m. and about 15 minutes before it was already in line. The restaurant is simple, but the food is a thousand note, so I found out why the queue. Enormous dishes, medium service, good price and excellent location. I loved to meet

reviews.title: A most unsatisfactory experience in Baranco
reviews.text:
To help celebrate my 80th birthday, my daughter did a lot of homework from her home in Calgary, searching for a good restaurant in Baranco, and three months ahead, and satisfied that Isolina would meet our needs, made a reservation for dinner for seven of my family on 7th February. She later  flew to Lima with her partner, to spend time with my wife and I.
On the date in question, we duly ordered a selection of dishes, including Osso Buco and Seco de Carne.
Only after we had all made significant progress eating, a few hints and comments arose about the degree of saltiness in seemingly every dish. Including, the beans, mashed potatoes, the rice and the salad, and most of all, the meat dishes. The family were reluctant to make comments in fear of spoiling the dinner, for all. Of course, by this time we had passed the point of no return, but we carried on regardless.
Before the waiter collected the remnants, I asked to speak to him, explaining our concerns and dissatisfaction, and asking for somebody in authority to sample the food remnants, in order to verify our concern. No comment was forthcoming, no excuse was made, and only on leaving did we get an opportunity to voice our concerns to the manager on duty, whom had little of substance to say except that they were trying to improve,
In all my years of living and visiting Peru with my Peruvian wife, I have never felt the need or urge to complain about food quality, but I must be frank in saying that the meal was the worst ever experienced.
But what was the most annoying issue, was that there was absolutely no hint of an apology or excuse. And it all made for an exceptionally distressing experience for my daughter, who had gone to such great lengths to make it all an enjoyable and memorable event.
I earnestly request that Management read these comments, and provide some form of comment on how this could occur in what might reasonably be expected in a restaurant that seemingly enjoys an otherwise a reasonable reputation, although I am not sure how.

reviews.title: Saw the lineup before the restaurant opened and glad we waited
reviews.text:
We loved our lunch at this charming restaurant in Barranco.    We walked past the side entrance and saw a long line of people waiting for the restaurant to open for lunch.   My husband stood in the lineup while I walked around this interesting area.   We got a table pretty quickly as most people wanted to be seated inside.    
We had an amazing lunch.  My husband had the traditional Peruvian  pork sandwich and I ordered the ceviche with yellow Amarillo pepper sauce.   Not only were our meals very beautifully presented but they tasted amazing.   The ceviche was delicious.   Very happy we stood inline and had a meal here.   If we had have been in Barranco another time, we would have eaten here again!   Great service as well.

reviews.title: Still great and really good value
reviews.text: What a cracking place. The plate serves are very large but they have what they refer to as personal serves - so if want to share get a normal serve but otherwise the personal plates are the way to go. The lomo saltado and rice dishes we had were both very good. The place is very popular and by the time we left people were queuing to get in. Service was excellent - precise, prompt and helpful re dish choices. Go here for quality cuisine and great value. But make sure you do not over order given serving  sizes.

reviews.title: Traditional and popular restaurant
reviews.text:
This restaurant is very hyped and the atmosphere there is warm and buzzing. It is very popular and there seems to be a line there at all times, so do book your table in advance if you want to visit! We unfortunately couldn't do that since our schedule in Lima was unclear. We decided to give it a shot anyway and were pleased when we did get a table outside (was pretty chilly in the evening, but that's on us).
 Service was friendly but not as attentive as we already had gotten a little used too in Lima. Out of the two dishes we ordered one was a little disappointing, mostly for lack of seasoning. Also, the wine we ordered was definitely not the best, drinkable. 
Overall not a bad experience, but for this price and much lower you can get such delicious food in this city, we were perhaps expecting a bit more.

reviews.title: Regular
reviews.text:
Hello, the restaurant has always been my favorite and I go whenever I can. However, I must mention that the chicken pepper was quite salty, as was the accompanying rice.

On the other hand, we understand that it is a house and that those who visit the local Barranco do it because we like the place, but the restaurant is not exactly economical, so the hygienic services should be in better condition.

Yesterday, in the women's room, there was no light; only a lamp that barely illuminated. In addition, the toilet had traces of everything, apparently due to lack of water. When trying to wash my hands, I encountered a similar problem: almost no water was falling. The bathroom door was also broken at the bottom.

I believe that, because of the restaurant’s reputation (which doesn’t just depend on its food), it is important to take care of all the details of the services to make the experience really good.

reviews.title: Poor gastronomic experience in Lima
reviews.text:
We arrived at the restaurant after several indications.
But it was a big disappointment: starting with a menu with few options, waiters with poor and time-consuming care.
The food was the worst part of the experience. No taste, we ordered a ceviche that included fried pulp. We've never eaten a dough that hard and tasteless.
Much fame and bad quality.
No recommend

reviews.title: Go somewhere else
reviews.text: My reservation was for Friday, January 10 2025 for 2 people at 7pm, reservation was under my name. (Isolina Barranco 2nd floor) we had a terrible experience, we requested to speak to a manager cause the table next to us was meant to be for 4 people, and they had 7 people seating there waiting for a bigger table to be made, this was a safety issue, and people that were going to the restrooms kept hitting me every time they  pass, the so called manager named Geraldine refused to correct the issue, and  made up a story. Food was ok, but i’ll never be back for sure. I request upper management to look into this issue, our waitress admitted the manager made a mistake.

reviews.title: Pure salt. Is quantity not quality
reviews.text: Polo's place. Only quantity not quality. Your pickle of pretty salty. Looks like the cook dropped the salt bowl on the plate. The best waters I had at the end.

reviews.title: Isolita top choice
reviews.text: Isolina is a classic lime home-cooked and delicious food the prices are a bit high but worth that if the queue is very long..

reviews.title: Too much waiting
reviews.text: On Sundays you can not make reservations, what a horror to have to queue and wait 2 hours and a half for lunch!! we ended up going to lunch at one of the thousands of extraordinary restaurants in Lima! how disorganized in Isolina, with a little order things would be better!

reviews.title: Emblematic Limeña Tavern.
reviews.text: On our tour of Barranco we visit Isolina, an emblematic restaurant of Peruvian cuisine. We can highlight its warm and welcoming atmosphere, with a decoration that highlights the traditional character. Isolina offers an authentic culinary experience that evokes the homemade flavors of Peruvian cuisine and that reflect its rich culinary tradition. In Isolina you can try the typical dishes of Peru as the limestone cause and the tiraditos with a modern touch, fusing tradition and modernity in a delicious way, the cocktails also stand out for their variety and flavor. It is an ideal place for those looking to enjoy the authentic flavors of Peruvian cuisine and have a special time.

reviews.title: A bit overrated family style meals
reviews.text:
Went there for dinner on a Sunday evening. Short wait and overall quick service. Got apps and dinner no drinks. 

The apps were solid. Had the civiche and it was awesome. Great flavors and the fried octopus in it was incredible. 

Dinners are huge and meant to be family style. We were not really warned of this and ordered 3 meals for a family of 5 after 3 apps thinking we would go light. The food could have easily fed 10 for dinner. We barely ate half. 

Had the osobucco  special. Taste was bland and meat was some of the toughest osobucco I’ve had.  Also had the fried rice dish which was really good. Highly recommend this one. Also had the shredded chicken stew which was so so. Flavor was good but a lot of gravy on it. 

I feel that overall the restaurant is a bit overrated for all of the hype and recommendations.

reviews.title: Improve the coordination of orders so that food comes out together.
reviews.text: The food's good, I ordered a ceviche and a bread with chicharrón. I wanted to eat together with my friend and it turns out that the ceviche arrived first and 10/15 minutes later my bread with chicharrón arrived. That doesn't make sense, people win to eat together not to see how the other eats. And yes, there was a problem at least to warn, but it wasn't my case.

reviews.title: 100% recommended, vegetarian options very good
reviews.text: We went to dinner at the recommendation of a friend and exceeded our expectations. Nick the waiter very friendly and attentive at all times. Large portions, the best rocoto we tasted. There were 4-5 vegetarian options, the exquisite vegetarian cause. Recommended 100%.
